free_text.inst.v2.D8: Answered strictly from the documented public record: born 1 October 1924 in the Wise Sanitarium at Plains, Georgia (the first US president born in a hospital); Naval Academy 1943-46; married Rosalynn Smith 7 July 1946; four children (John William 1947, James Earl III 1950, Donnel Jeffrey 1952, Amy Lynn 1967); left the Navy in 1953 after his father Earl's death to take over the family peanut land and warehouse; Georgia state senate 1963-67, defeated for governor 1966, born-again turn 1967, Governor 1971-75, President 1977-81, defeated by Reagan November 1980; left office roughly a million dollars in debt from the warehouse and sold the business; founded the Carter Center in 1982 and taught at Emory; Nobel Peace Prize 2002; metastatic melanoma with liver and brain lesions in 2015, falls and brain surgery in 2019, home hospice from February 2023, Rosalynn's death November 2023. Part D was left blank on purpose - no reading was viewed, so there is nothing honest to say about it.

notes: Genuinely ambiguous points. A1/A2: 7:00 AM is the time carried in the astrological record with a birth-record rating; a careful biographer cannot say whether the source document was the hospital chart or the certificate, and a round hour on the hour is itself a sign of rounding. A10: Earl Carter is described everywhere as stern and admired rather than warm or hostile - 'distant but not hostile' is the closest fit, though Carter's own later writing shows real affection. A13: forced-choice - he lost ALL three siblings (Ruth 1983, Billy 1988, Gloria 1990), all to pancreatic cancer, and was also close to them, so 'lost' was chosen over 'close'. A15: his Union College nuclear-physics coursework and Rickover's reactor programme ended when his father died, but his formal degree path was uninterrupted, so 'no'. A17: honestly split - Navy, state senate, governorship and presidency were all public service, while the peanut business and the Carter Center were his own and both went well; 'about the same' is the defensible answer. A19: 'less than it deserved' reflects the widely documented one-term repudiation followed by later reappraisal and the 2002 Nobel; 'about right' is arguable. A21: no documented speculation, betting or personal share trading (assets went into a blind trust), hence 'never'. A31: 'briefly' refers to the documented despair after the 1966 gubernatorial defeat that preceded his 1967 born-again experience; there is no record of clinical treatment. A34: counted the four years at Annapolis plus seven years of naval service as institutional living, not confinement in the penal sense. A36: he was in home hospice from February 2023 and Rosalynn died that November, so the period after mid-2023 was much worse than the six years before it. C2: metastatic melanoma at 90 was grave, but he outlived the diagnosis by nine years and was healthy for the first nine decades, so 'gone well' on the long-term-illness axis. C6 was scored as difficulty on the strength of three siblings' early cancer deaths and the Billy Carter/Libya affair, notwithstanding Ruth's positive spiritual influence. Part D (D1-D7) omitted: those questions are about a reading, which this exercise did not and could not view.
